descriptionHtml:
Approach · OAT-01 Signing In & Session Security · S02 Signed out: only email codes get in, a wrong or reused code is refused, every route is gated, and a sign-in survives a reload

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U1 Sign-in is by email one-time passcode only: no password field and no shared or static PIN anywhere. The only exception is the two app review accounts, which use a fixed code. (UAT OAT-01 step 1; UAT OAT-01 Expected; TFA-94513 AC 1) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress
  • U3 After 12 hours idle, the physician has to sign in again with an email OTP. (UAT OAT-01 step 3; UAT OAT-01 Expected; TFA-94513 AC 4) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress
  • U2 After first login the session credential is kept in the device's secure keychain, and Face ID / fingerprint unlocks the app instead of a full re-login. … (UAT OAT-01 step 2; UAT OAT-01 Expected; TFA-94513 AC 3; TFA-94513 AC 17) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress

Test design technique: Equivalence classes (equivalence) — Check the same rule again with another class of input (Hospital / Nursing Home, other data); every class has to be right.

Given A signed-out browser (anonymous project) and DEMO_USER

When Open / and /reset-password?token=old; POST to each password and reset route under /api/auth; enter a wrong 6-digit code; use one valid code twice; open /rounding, /clinic, /snf, /rounding/sheet and /settings directly; sign in through the form, then reload.

Then Both pages show Send sign-in code and no Password field, Forgot or Sign up button. Every password route answers 404. The wrong code shows an alert and no list, and the second use of a code is refused. Every route shows the sign-in gate (the Email field), never the app. After a sign-in, a reload brings the list back without the sign-in screen.

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): auth.anon.spec.ts and login.anon.spec.ts assertions, judged against U1 (no password field anywhere; a code that works twice behaves like a static PIN), U3 (sign-in is actually required on every route, not just the landing page) and the web half of U2 (the session persists after first login; the unlock half is S19 and Q1).

Where it ran: local newspec-a (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S02 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-01.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 25acd727 (10-15/16/17 re-tests), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-a.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: API · API (Convex functions) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-a.

UAT item: OAT-01 Signing In & Session Security · Section: B · Operational Acceptance Tests · Scenario: OAT-01/S02

Tickets: TFA-94513 Signing In & Session Security (in progress)

New local lane newspec-a: status passed in newspec-a/results.json → passed (passed).

How it is tested (newspec-a/plan.json, automatable: yes): Tim's six existing titles in auth.anon.spec.ts / login.anon.spec.ts exist on main; run them with --project=anonymous (the only gap was spec-matrix.mjs not passing that project). Verdict = the Playwright assertions. — Existing deterministic specs; the runner just never selected the anonymous project.

Detail:

Tim's six titles run with --project=anonymous: 6/6 pass (only email codes on / and /reset-password?token=old; all 9 password routes 404; wrong code refused with an alert; a code works once; /rounding /clinic /snf /rounding/sheet /settings gated; sign-in survives a reload). These use DEMO_USER (existing tests, not new). Collision risk: these titles sign in and issue codes for the shared DEMO_USER (the matrix requires it); a parallel job using DEMO_USER can invalidate their codes, so run S02 when no other job uses that account.

Evidence: 1 attached.

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane A runs Tim's Playwright specs, which sign in their own fixture accounts and need the admin key; dev has neither (runner-contract §10), so this runs on the local stack only (Quinn 2026-10-14).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
